seo.meta_title: Is Sakura Japanese Steakhouse a Chain? Sakura Hibachi Guide
seo.meta_description: Sakura is a Virginia-born hibachi chain founded in 1988, but many unrelated restaurants also use the name. How to tell them apart and what hibachi costs.
seo.h1: Is Sakura Japanese Steakhouse a Chain?

question: Is Sakura Japanese Steakhouse a Chain?
quick_answer: Partly. There is a Sakura Japanese Steak & Seafood House chain, founded in 1988 by Marc Ha in Fredericksburg, Virginia, with about 20 locations mainly in Virginia, Maryland and New Jersey, plus a few in California. But "Sakura," which means cherry blossom in Japanese, is also one of the most common names for independent hibachi and sushi restaurants across the U.S., and most of those have no connection to the chain. Menus and prices vary from one Sakura to the next.
key_facts: Sakura chain founded in 1988 by Marc Ha
About 20 chain locations, mostly VA, MD and NJ
Many unrelated restaurants share the name
Hibachi dinners usually include soup and salad

body.heading: The Sakura chain
body.text: Sakura Japanese Steak & Seafood House was founded in 1988 by Marc Ha, who opened his first restaurant in Fredericksburg, Virginia, with just seven hibachi tables. The chain grew to around 19 to 20 locations, mostly in Virginia, Maryland and New Jersey, and has also expanded to California. Its restaurants offer teppanyaki tables, a sushi bar and a traditional Japanese menu, though the menu varies by location. A Sakura location in Camden County, New Jersey, opened more recently.

body.heading: Why there are so many Sakuras
body.text: Sakura is the Japanese word for cherry blossom, a symbol of Japan, so it's a popular name for Japanese restaurants. You'll find independent restaurants called Sakura Japanese Steakhouse, Sakura Hibachi or Sakura Garden in places like North Dakota, Texas, Ohio and Connecticut. These are usually locally owned and have their own menus and prices, even if their names and hibachi shows look similar.

body.heading: How to tell if your Sakura is part of the chain
body.text: Check the restaurant's website. Chain locations usually mention Marc Ha or the 1988 Fredericksburg origin, and they're concentrated in the Mid-Atlantic. A Sakura outside those states, with its own standalone website or no website, is most likely independent. Gift cards and promotions usually only work within the same owner's restaurants.

body.heading: What a Sakura hibachi dinner includes
body.text: At most Sakura restaurants, a hibachi dinner is cooked on a flat-top grill at your table by a chef who puts on a show, and it comes with soup, salad, grilled vegetables and fried rice or noodles. Typical prices on a representative Sakura menu are about $16.99 for hibachi chicken, $23.99 for steak and $25.99 for filet mignon, with combination dinners from about $24.99 to $51. Sushi rolls run about $6 to $13. See our Sakura menu for a full price list.

body.heading: Similar hibachi restaurants
body.text: If you don't have a Sakura nearby, Benihana is the best-known national hibachi chain. Many towns also have independent hibachi steakhouses. Prices and portions at independent restaurants vary, so check the local menu.
